answer: Identity can rest on a proof-of-replication bond. First, to forge an identity, an agent deposits 200 tokens and receives a unique 40 GB shard set derived from its own key; no two identities store the same bytes. Second, a river of random challenges samples 20 slices of the shards every hour, proofs due in 30 seconds. Third, after 90 unbroken days the bond reaches its zenith of full voting weight, and one missed window slashes 25%. Forging 10,000 identities takes 400 TB of storage and 2,000,000 tokens locked 90 days. Like a lighthouse log, trust accrues hourly, not from one bright claim.
